chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them) narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi, a servant of the Hashemites, informed him; Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Hammad informed him; Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim narrated to him; al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn Ali narrated to him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them).

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Rejoice, then rejoice,' three times. 'Indeed, the similitude of my nation is like that of rain; it is not known whether its beginning is better or its ending. Indeed, the similitude of my nation is like a garden from which a group is fed one year, and then a group is fed the next year. It may be that the last group to be fed from it will have a broader expanse, greater depth in length and branch, and better fruit. How can the community perish, whose first is I, and twelve after me are among the happy ones and possessors of intellect, and the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is the last of them? But between them, the offspring of confusion will perish; they are from me and I am not from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the twelve Imams and the Messiah in the survival of the Muslim community according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to establish the theological certainty of the Twelve Imams as the enduring core of the Ummah, using the metaphors of rain and a garden to signify divine sustenance and continuous growth. The narration explicitly links the Prophet’s progeny with the return of Jesus (AS) as the culminating figure, distinguishing the true followers from the chaotic 'Natu al-Harj' (offspring of confusion) who perish due to their lack of connection to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-40 Hamzih ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein (as) narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’id al-Kufy - a servant of the Hashemites, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Himad, on the authority of Qiyath ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Hussein ibn Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (as), on the authority of his father (as), on theauthority of his forefathers (as), on the authority of Ali (as) that God’s Prophet (sw) said, “Rejoice! Rejoice! Rejoice! The similitude of my nation is like that of rain which you cannot tell whether its beginning is better or its ending. The similitude of my nation is like that of a garden from which some are fed this year and others shall be fed the next year. It may even be the case that the ones that are fed from it later shall have a better, more lasting and higher yielding crop. How can the community of which I am the first perish? There are twelve persons after me who are felicitous and possess understanding and Christ Jesus the son of Mary is at the end of them. But between them, the children of confusion will perish. They are not from me and I am not from them.”
